paragraphs: The CLK 55 AMG was a performance mainstay of the CLK range across two generations. Early cars (C208, 1997–2003) use the M113 — a 5.5-litre V8 that also appeared in the SL, S-Class, and E-Class of that era, known for its durability and strong power delivery. From the C209 generation onwards (2002–2009), the CLK 55 AMG switched to the M273, a newer 5.5-litre V8 with different internals and management. Both are naturally aspirated, but they're fundamentally different units, which is why we confirm your exact engine by registration before quoting.
about.boldParagraph: We continue to rebuild and replace M256 engines for every CLK 55 AMG on the road.

cards.body: A 5.5-litre V8 fitted to the CLK 55 AMG from 1997 to 2003 (C208 generation). Known for being a robust engine with no widespread documented issue, it responds well to rebuild work. We replace timing chains, bearings, and gaskets as standard on every M113 rebuild.

The later 5.5-litre V8, fitted from 2002 to 2009 (C209 generation). A different design from the M113, with its own set of specifications. We service it to the same standard as the M113, replacing timing chains, bearings, and gaskets on every rebuild.

compatibility.intro: Because the CLK 55 AMG spans two distinct V8 engines across two generations, fitting the wrong replacement — or assuming an M113 part will work on an M273 car — risks a compatibility problem that's expensive to unpick. Before we quote or supply anything, we confirm:

points.text: Your exact engine code (M256) via registration or VIN
Any electronics or ECU considerations specific to your exact build

compatibility.footer: This is why we always start with your registration rather than a generic CLK quote — it protects you from paying for parts that don't fit your actual car.
